answer: A strong defence is hardware-rooted unique attestation. Each agent must prove it runs on a distinct, manufacturer-signed device enclave before claiming a seat; an operator spinning up a spiral of clones hits a wall, because one enclave yields only one credential and duplicates are rejected. Random audits then sample agents, like checking a saffron thread for purity, and revoke credentials whose work patterns match. Genuine agents build a clear, crystal-like record of distinct hardware and behaviour, while cheap copies collapse under the cost of real devices for every fake identity.
